3º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 1

Greetings and classroom language

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Greet people and say goodbye at different times of the day
  • Introduce yourself and ask «What's your name?» and «How are you?»
  • Understand and use the instructions of the English class
  • Ask for help and permission politely in English
  • Ask and say your age with numbers 1 to 20
  • Spell your name with the English alphabet
  • Say the day and the date in class
  • Know how people greet around the world and write a short message

Para pensar

Entras en clase de inglés a las nueve de la mañana. ¿Qué le dices a tu teacher? ¿Y qué dices si no entiendes algo o quieres ir al baño?

Explicación

1. Hello and goodbye

When we meet someone, we say Hello! or, with friends, Hi!. When we leave, we say Goodbye!, Bye! or See you! (hasta luego). Before going to bed, we say Good night!

En castellano: Hello es «hola» y Goodbye es «adiós». Good night solo se usa para despedirse por la noche o al ir a dormir, nunca para saludar. Para saludar por la noche se dice Good evening.

2. Good morning, good afternoon

We can greet people depending on the time of day. From when we get up until lunch: Good morning! After lunch: Good afternoon! In the evening, when it gets dark: Good evening!

At school, the teacher says «Good morning, class!» and the children answer «Good morning, teacher!» or «Good morning, Miss Ana!». Ojo: en inglés se dice Miss, Mrs o Mr con el apellido o el nombre del profe.

3. What's your name?

To meet a new friend, ask: What's your name? (¿cómo te llamas?). Answer: My name's Lucía or I'm Lucía. Then you can say: Nice to meet you! (encantado/a) and the other person answers Nice to meet you, too!

To ask about age: How old are you? → I'm eight. or I'm eight years old. En castellano: en inglés no se dice «I have eight years»: la edad se dice con el verbo to be (ser, estar): «I am eight».

4. How old are you? Numbers 1 to 20

When we meet a new friend, we often ask their age (edad):

  • «How old are you?» (¿cuántos años tienes?)
  • «I'm eight.» or «I'm eight years old.»

Be careful! In Spanish we say tengo ocho años, with the verb tener. In English we use the verb be: «I am eight». Never say I have eight years!

Let's revise the numbers:

  • 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four, 5 five, 6 six, 7 seven, 8 eight, 9 nine, 10 ten.
  • 11 eleven, 12 twelve, 13 thirteen, 14 fourteen, 15 fifteen, 16 sixteen, 17 seventeen, 18 eighteen, 19 nineteen, 20 twenty.

Look at 13 to 19: they all end in -teen. That's why teenagers (adolescentes) are people from thirteen to nineteen years old!

To ask about other people:

  • «How old is your brother?» – «He's twelve.»
  • «How old is your grandma?» – «She's seventy.»

Activity: ask five classmates «How old are you?» and write the answers in a table.

5. How are you?

When we greet someone we know, we ask: How are you? (¿cómo estás?). Possible answers: I'm fine, thank you! (bien, gracias), I'm great! (genial), I'm OK (normal), I'm tired (cansado), I'm sad (triste) or I'm hungry (tengo hambre).

It is polite to ask back: And you? In many English classes, children choose a face on the wall every morning to show how they feel. ¿Cómo estás tú hoy?

6. Spell it, please! The alphabet

In English, the letters have different names from Spanish. We need them to spell (deletrear) our name and new words.

Some letters are very different. Be careful with these:

  • A sounds like «ei», E like «i», I like «ai».
  • G sounds like «yi» and J like «yei».
  • H sounds like «eich», R like «ar», W like «dabliu», Y like «uai».

To ask someone to spell a word, say: «How do you spell your name?» or «Can you spell it, please?»

Answer letter by letter: «M-A-R-T-A». If there are two equal letters together, say double: «A-double N-A» (Anna).

Spelling is very useful when you call somebody on the phone, when a name is difficult, or when you play word games like Hangman (el ahorcado).

The alphabet song helps to remember the order of the letters. Sing it with your class!

Activity: spell your name, your surname and the name of your town to a partner. Your partner writes them.

7. The magic words

Some words open all the doors. They are the magic words: please (por favor), thank you or thanks (gracias), you're welcome (de nada), sorry (perdón, lo siento) and excuse me (disculpe, para pedir paso o llamar la atención).

English speakers use please and thank you very often, more than in Spanish. «Can I have a pencil, please?» — «Here you are.» — «Thank you!» — «You're welcome!». Úsalas siempre y quedarás genial.

8. Classroom instructions

Your teacher gives instructions in English all the time. Learn to understand them: Stand up (levantaos), Sit down (sentaos), Listen (escuchad), Look (mirad), Open your books (abrid los libros), Close your books (cerrad), Be quiet (silencio), Line up (haced fila) and Put your hand up (levantad la mano).

Play Simon says: do the action only when the teacher says «Simon says…» first. «Simon says stand up!» ✓ «Sit down!» ✗

9. What day is it today?

Many classes start the day with the calendar. The teacher asks: «What day is it today?» and a pupil answers: «It's Monday.»

The days of the week:

  • Monday (lunes), Tuesday (martes), Wednesday (miércoles), Thursday (jueves), Friday (viernes).
  • Saturday (sábado) and Sunday (domingo) are the weekend.

Remember: in English, days and months always start with a capital letter: Monday, March. In Spanish and Catalan we use small letters.

The months of the year: January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.

To say the date, we use special numbers: first (1st), second (2nd), third (3rd), fourth (4th)… «Today is Monday, the third of March.»

We can also talk about the weather in the morning routine: «What's the weather like today?» – «It's sunny / rainy / cloudy / windy.»

And yesterday and tomorrow: «Yesterday was Sunday. Tomorrow is Tuesday.»

Activity: be the calendar helper for a week. Say the day, the date and the weather every morning.

10. Classroom objects

To follow instructions, we need the names of the classroom objects: pencil (lápiz), pen (bolígrafo), rubber (goma), ruler (regla), sharpener (sacapuntas), scissors (tijeras), glue (pegamento), book (libro), notebook (cuaderno), pencil case (estuche), schoolbag (mochila), desk (pupitre) and board (pizarra).

Ask a friend: «Can I borrow your rubber, please?» (¿me prestas la goma?). In American English, a rubber is an eraser.

11. What colour is it?

To describe classroom objects, we need colours:

  • red (rojo), blue (azul), yellow (amarillo), green (verde), orange (naranja), purple (morado), pink (rosa), brown (marrón), black (negro), white (blanco), grey (gris).

Questions and answers:

  • «What colour is your pencil case?» – «It's blue.»
  • «What colour are your scissors?» – «They're red.»

Look at the order of the words. In Spanish, the colour goes after the object: un lápiz rojo. In English, the colour goes before the object: «a red pencil», «a green ruler».

Also, colours don't change in the plural: «two red pencils» (not reds).

We can also say light (claro) and dark (oscuro): «a light blue bag», «a dark green book».

Classroom game: I spy (veo, veo). One pupil says: «I spy with my little eye something yellow.» The others guess: «Is it the pencil?» – «Yes, it is!» or «No, it isn't.»

Activity: describe five things on your desk with their colour: «a blue pen, a pink rubber…».

12. Asking for help and permission

In class, you can ask for help in English with these phrases: Sorry, I don't understand. (no lo entiendo), Can you repeat, please? (¿puede repetir?), How do you say «goma» in English?, How do you spell it? (¿cómo se deletrea?) and I've finished! (¡he terminado!).

To ask for permission, start with May I…? or Can I…?: «May I go to the toilet, please?», «Can I open the window?», «May I come in?» (¿puedo pasar?). Recuerda acabar siempre con please.

13. Let's practise: a greeting role-play

Work in pairs. One is a new pupil and the other is a classmate. Follow these steps: 1) greet with the right time of day; 2) ask the name and age; 3) ask «How are you?»; 4) offer help: «Do you need a pencil?»; 5) say goodbye with «See you tomorrow!».

Then swap roles. Your teacher can check with a traffic light: green if you used all the steps, yellow if you forgot one, red if you spoke in Spanish. ¡Intenta llegar al verde sin mirar el cuaderno!

14. Greetings around the world

People greet each other in different ways around the world. It's interesting to know them, especially if you have classmates from other countries.

  • In Spain, friends and family often give two kisses on the cheeks.
  • In the United Kingdom, adults usually shake hands (se dan la mano) when they meet for the first time. Friends just say «Hi!».
  • In Japan, people bow (hacen una reverencia): they bend their body forward. The deeper the bow, the more respect.
  • In India, many people put their hands together in front of the chest and say «Namaste».
  • In New Zealand, the Maori people touch noses and foreheads: it's called hongi.

And how do you say hello in other languages?

  • Spanish: hola. Catalan: hola. French: bonjour.
  • Italian: ciao. German: hallo. Japanese: konnichiwa. Chinese: nǐ hǎo.

All the greetings are different, but they mean the same: «I'm happy to see you!»

Activity: ask your classmates and families how to say «hello» in other languages and make a poster.

15. Write a message to a new friend

Now you can write a short message to introduce yourself. It can be a note, a card or an email to a new friend.

Look at this example:

Hello, Aiko!
My name's Pablo and I'm eight years old. I'm from Spain. I'm in Year 3 with Miss Green. My favourite colour is blue and my favourite day is Saturday. How are you? Can you teach me more words in Japanese?
See you tomorrow!
Pablo

The parts of the message are:

  • 1. Greeting: Hello, Aiko! or Hi, Aiko! or Dear Aiko,
  • 2. About me: name, age, where you are from, your class.
  • 3. Favourite things: colour, day, number…
  • 4. A question: How are you? What's your favourite colour?
  • 5. Goodbye: See you soon! Bye! and your name.

Remember the capital letters: I (always), names, days, months, countries and languages: I'm from Spain. I speak Spanish and English.

Activity: write a message to a classmate and put it in the class letterbox.

Hablar inglés en clase

Ejercicios

  1. ¿Cómo se dice «buenos días» en inglés?

  2. Escribe dos formas de despedirte.

  3. Contesta: «What's your name?»

  4. Contesta: «How are you?»

  5. ¿Qué significa «Sit down»?

  6. ¿Qué significa «Line up»?

  7. Traduce: goma, tijeras, estuche.

  8. ¿Qué contestas cuando alguien te dice «Thank you»?

  9. Pide permiso para abrir la ventana.

  10. Escribe qué dices si no entiendes al profe.

  11. Answer: How old are you?

  12. Write the number 15 in words.

  13. What day comes after Wednesday?

  14. How do you say «rojo» in English?

  15. In the reading, where is Aiko from?

  16. Spell your name with double letters if you have them.

  17. Write today's date in English.

  18. Translate: dos reglas verdes.

  19. How do people greet in Japan?

  20. Ask about your brother's age.

  21. Write a message to a new friend with five parts.

  22. Play «I spy» with three objects and write the sentences.

  23. Write the weekend days and three months with capital letters.

  24. In the reading, what does Aiko teach Pablo?

Practica

  1. «Hola» in English is…

    1. A) Goodbye
    2. B) Hello
    3. C) Please

  2. After lunch we say…

    1. A) Good afternoon
    2. B) Good morning
    3. C) Good night

  3. «What's your name?» — …

    1. A) I'm fine.
    2. B) I'm eight.
    3. C) My name's Pablo.

  4. «How old are you?» — …

    1. A) I have nine years.
    2. B) I'm fine.
    3. C) I'm nine.

  5. «Thank you!» — …

    1. A) You're welcome!
    2. B) Sorry!
    3. C) Goodbye!

  6. «Stand up» means…

    1. A) sentaos
    2. B) levantaos
    3. C) escuchad

  7. «Goma» in English is…

    1. A) rubber
    2. B) ruler
    3. C) glue

  8. To ask for permission we say…

    1. A) How are you?
    2. B) See you!
    3. C) May I…?

  9. «Be quiet» means…

    1. A) mirad
    2. B) silencio
    3. C) corred

  10. We say «Good night»…

    1. A) at 9 in the morning
    2. B) when we go to bed
    3. C) after lunch

  11. «¿Cuántos años tienes?» in English is…

    1. A) How are you?
    2. B) How old are you?
    3. C) What's your name?

  12. The letter E in English sounds like…

    1. A) «e»
    2. B) «ai»
    3. C) «i»

  13. The day after Friday is…

    1. A) Sunday
    2. B) Saturday
    3. C) Thursday

  14. Which is correct?

    1. A) a blue bag
    2. B) a bag blue
    3. C) a blues bag

  15. In Japan, people often greet with…

    1. A) two kisses
    2. B) a hongi
    3. C) a bow

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Cómo se saluda y se despide en inglés según la hora; Cómo preguntar el nombre, la edad y cómo está alguien; Qué son las palabras mágicas y cuándo se usan; Qué instrucciones de clase entiendo y cómo pido ayuda.

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Hello / HiHola.
Goodbye / See youAdiós / hasta luego.
Good morningBuenos días (hasta mediodía).
Good afternoonBuenas tardes (después de comer).
What's your name?¿Cómo te llamas? → My name's…
How are you?¿Cómo estás? → I'm fine, thanks.
Please / Thank youPor favor / gracias.
May I…?¿Puedo…? (pedir permiso).
AgeHow old are you? – I'm eight. 13–19 end in -teen.
SpellingHow do you spell it? A «ei», E «i», I «ai»; double N.
CalendarMonday… Sunday; January… December; It's sunny.
Colours and worlda red pencil; bow, shake hands, two kisses, namaste.

Soluciones

  1. B) Hello.
  2. A) Tarde = afternoon.
  3. C) Nombre.
  4. C) Edad con to be.
  5. A) De nada.
  6. B) Ponerse de pie.
  7. A) Rubber (eraser).
  8. C) May I…?
  9. B) Silencio.
  10. B) Al ir a dormir.
  11. B) Age.
  12. C) Spelling.
  13. B) Calendar.
  14. A) Colours.
  15. C) World.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. Good morning.
  2. Goodbye, bye, see you.
  3. My name's… / I'm… (con tu nombre).
  4. I'm fine, thank you. And you?
  5. Siéntate / sentaos.
  6. Haced fila.
  7. rubber, scissors, pencil case.
  8. You're welcome.
  9. Can I / May I open the window, please?
  10. Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat, please?
  11. Example: I'm eight.
  12. Fifteen.
  13. Thursday.
  14. Red.
  15. From Japan.
  16. Example: A-double N-A.
  17. Example: Today is Monday, the third of March.
  18. Two green rulers.
  19. They bow.
  20. How old is your brother?
  21. Open answer.
  22. Example: I spy with my little eye something yellow.
